text:
alex: Heads-up — after landing commit abc123 we see a regression in tail latency on the KV-heavy repro. 95th went from ~45ms to ~70ms on the 2-worker bench.
jamie: Ugh. repro command + traces?
alex: repro is bench/repro_kv_thrash.py (small seqs, random prefixes). attached nsys + perfetto from both before/after on the same machine.
perf-bot: Upload complete: https://perf.redwood.local/traces/1729309876 (before) and /traces/1729309877 (after) :white_check_mark:
priya: Quick skim of perfetto timeline — after commit we get frequent kernel-switching at the end of each step. kernels: matmul_small -> matmul_large -> memcpy, repeated. That memcpy tail looks new.
ben: That smells like kernel selection flip where a different matmul variant emits longer host<->device copies. Any change to selection thresholds?
alex: Yes, the commit bumped evict_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.7 to avoid early evictions. Might be causing more cache misses + larger KV fetches.
jamie: Could be thrashing: larger fetches mean more memcopies and more kernel fallback. timeline shows ~3.2ms extra memcpy per token in after trace.
alex: nsys summary snippet (after):

    CUDA Activity:  total time 1.2s
    memcpy HtoD  count 540  total 1.73s  avg 3.2ms
    kernel matmul_large  count 540  total 0.72s

and (before):

    memcpy HtoD  count 420  total 0.63s  avg 1.5ms
    kernel matmul_large  count 420  total 0.55s

priya: Also saw more frequent KV cache evictions in logs: lines like "kv:evict idx=... reason=threshold" spiking after the change.
ben: Can we reproduce with a tight bisect script? i.e. build+run repro and fail if 95th > 60ms. If so, git bisect will isolate commit.
jamie: I'll drop a bisect script. Suggested pattern:

    #!/bin/bash
    set -e
    make -j
    python3 bench/repro_kv_thrash.py --iters 200 --warmup 20 --workers 2 > /tmp/repro.out
    p95=$(jq -r .p95 < /tmp/repro.out)
    echo "p95=$p95"
    if (( $(echo "$p95 > 60" | bc -l) )); then
      exit 1
    else
      exit 0
    fi

priya: For profiling, use these commands to get comparable traces:

    nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_after -t cuda,osrt --sample=none --trace=cuda,kernel --capture-range=nvtx
    python3 bench/repro_kv_thrash.py --iters 200 --annotate-nvtx

and perfetto command (on target):

    perfetto -c perfetto_config.pbtxt -o /data/trace_after.pbz

perfetto config example (short):

    buffers: { size_kb: 10240 }
    data_sources: { config { name: "linux.ftrace" } }
    data_sources: { config { name: "gpu.counters" } }

ben: Also add --log-kv=true to repro to capture eviction timestamps; we can correlate with memcpy spikes on perfetto lanes.
alex: Ran a targeted run switching evict_threshold back to 0.6 locally — tail drops back to ~47ms. So likely culprit.
jamie: Great — bisect should find the exact commit range. Priya, can you do a quick top-of-stack flame for after trace and upload? helps us see if memcpy is lining up with kv fetch callsites.
priya: Uploaded flame: https://perf.redwood.local/flames/1729309888. Memcpy hotspots point at kv_fetch_async -> fill_buffer -> cudaMemcpyAsync.
ben: If kv_fetch_async is pulling bigger blobs, we need an early-size-shortcut in selection that prefers smaller fragments when batch concurrency high.
alex: For immediate mitigation I propose reverting the threshold bump for the next canary. I'll open a PR with the revert + test.
jamie: +1. Also add a regression test: synthetic bench that asserts no >25% p95 regression across builds.
perf-bot: New PR created: #5123 (revert: kv evict threshold) — https://git.redwood/repo/pull/5123 :rocket:
alex: Thanks all — next steps: jamie runs bisect to confirm, ben/priya to propose long-term fix (size-aware fetch heuristics), I'll push revert to canary.
ben: I'll sketch a patch to make fetches cap at 256KB when concurrent > 4.
priya: Will include perfetto/nvtx hooks in the repro so future bisects produce traces automatically.
alex: If anyone finds other oddness in the traces ping me. I'll wait for bisect results before merging revert. :eyes:
